question: A team lead is writing a short local practice note to sit underneath the company-wide AI standard. Which two items genuinely belong in it? Select two.
options: A) Who to contact when a situation arises that the company-wide AI standard does not clearly cover.
B) Which categories of team data must never be pasted into Claude under any circumstances at all.
C) The exact number of days for which the vendor keeps stored conversations before removal.
D) A ranked list telling each team member which model tier they should prefer for all of their own work.
E) A target for the number of working hours that every team member should save each week using Claude.
correct_answers: A) Who to contact when a situation arises that the company-wide AI standard does not clearly cover.
B) Which categories of team data must never be pasted into Claude under any circumstances at all.
explanations: Correct for a different reason: a named escalation contact is what stops people improvising when the standard runs out.
Correct. A local note is where the general standard becomes concrete about the specific data this team actually handles.
Retention periods are vendor facts that change and are documented by the vendor; copying a number into a team note invites it to go stale.
Model choice is a task-fit judgment made per piece of work, not a governance rule to assign per person.
A savings target pressures people towards using Claude and belongs to performance management, not to a governance note.
